solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sidekick managed church instead of shed

indicators.note: says one set of letters takes the place of another inside the longer word

parts.note: to have managed something is to have accomplished it
the word shed is taken as written, as the letters swapped out
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A helper who ran a church rather than a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of' swaps SHED out of ACCOMPLISHED and puts CE in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a partner or helper, often one assisting in a crime.

clue.text: Old ship formerly carrying rare freight out of Cuba

indicators.note: signals one letter being taken away from the longer word

parts.note: freight is goods carried, a cargo
C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

explanation.surface: A vessel that once shipped exotic goods away from Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formerly carrying rare' is colour that extends the definition: the Argo carried the Golden Fleece, a rare freight indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the legendary vessel of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Tea-time talk

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal conversation, a casual talk.

clue.text: Nice girl produced wine, I gathered

parts.note: produced means made

indicators.note: the wine gathers the I, holding it within its letters

parts.note: Moselle is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A pleasant young woman made wine, so I understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, hiding behind the adjective: a girl from Nice is a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: French term for an unmarried young woman, fitting a girl in Nice, France.

clue.text: Fast Othello finale? On the contrary

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rapid ending to Othello? No, quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: 'On the contrary' means the opposite of 'Fast', i.e. slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the musical direction for slow, the contrary of fast.

clue.text: Couples regularly surveyed back roads going nowhere

indicators.note: taking every other letter of Couples, at regular intervals
the word for surveyed is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to case a place is to survey it before a burglary

explanation.surface: Pairs often looked over back lanes that lead nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Cased is criminal slang: to case a joint is to survey it before a burglary. 'back' reverses that word to give the French-looking ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead-end streets, closed at one end, so they lead nowhere.

clue.text: Fly over and trace old Chinese house

indicators.note: in an across clue, over signals the insect's name turned back to front

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: An insect hovers above and marks out an ancient Chinese home.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'trace' is a further definition, a tang being a slight trace of flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tang was a Chinese imperial dynasty, and a dynasty is a royal house.

clue.text: See boss teasing man on board

parts.note: arch means playfully teasing or mischievous
a bishop is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: Look, the boss is ribbing a member of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb: a see is a bishop's diocese, so its boss is the senior cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop heads an archdiocese, the principal see of a province.

clue.text: Reaction to cold in Gander?

parts.note: a gander is a male goose, so its skin when chilled would literally be goose skin

explanation.walkthrough: Gander is also a town in Newfoundland, famously cold, which steers the solver toward geography.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumpy skin raised by cold or fear, named after a plucked bird's skin.

clue.text: Impressive cryptic clue about northern relative

parts.note: grand means impressive or magnificent

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the N, enclosing it
cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the word clue is jumbled

explanation.surface: A splendid puzzle clue that refers to someone from the north and their family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges CLUE to UCLE, and 'about' wraps those letters round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother of one's grandparent is a family member, hence a relative.

clue.text: "The Nymph", late Chopin piece, forerunner of foxtrot

indicators.note: a piece of the words, a run of letters lifted from them

explanation.surface: A late Chopin work titled The Nymph led into a foxtrot.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'forerunner of foxtrot' is another definition, as Echo comes just before Foxtrot in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Echo was a mountain nymph doomed to repeat others' words.

clue.text: Question: is romance ruined when it is boring?

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the word for it goes inside the jumble
ruined says the letters of is romance are wrecked and remade

parts.note: it is a coy euphemism for sex, as in having it

explanation.surface: Asking whether love is spoilt once intimacy becomes dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as a euphemism for sex is a long-standing convention; 'boring' here means drilling into the jumble from 'ruined', not tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross-examine is to question a witness closely, as in court.

clue.text: Hard to assess one MP on breadline, sadly not elected

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: sadly says the remaining letters are put into a sorry new order
not says the letters for elected are left out

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: It is difficult to judge a member of Parliament living in poverty who lost his seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from BREADLINE, leaving BREADLE, which 'sadly' rearranges to DERABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whose weight or effect cannot be measured or estimated in advance.

clue.text: Dash round shopping centre for contract details?

indicators.note: the run goes round the mall, enclosing it

parts.note: a dash is a short sprint
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Racing round the mall to find the terms of an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: the fine print is the sort of contract detail you may miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms printed tiny at the foot of an agreement, often conditions easily overlooked.

clue.text: Top surgeon's job in theatre blocking UV treatment

indicators.note: the theatre word sits within the treatment word, blocking it

parts.note: tanning is exposure to ultraviolet light
rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A senior surgeon's work in the operating theatre is halted during a sunbed session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is not a rank: it means the head, so this is surgery on the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring a hole in the skull is an operation on the top of the body.

clue.text: Dancing girl nearly stops exotic Madras carnival

indicators.note: the dancing letters stop up the city letters, going inside
exotic says the letters of the city are put into an unfamiliar order
dancing sets the letters moving into a new order
nearly means the word girl lacks its final letter

explanation.surface: A dancer almost halts a colourful festival in Madras.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate jumbles: 'Dancing' works on the shortened girl, 'exotic' on the Indian city, and 'stops' plugs the first into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive Shrove Tuesday celebration, famously a carnival in New Orleans and Rio.

clue.text: Contest concerning amateur people

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
lay means non-professional, as in a lay person
a race is a people of shared descent

explanation.surface: A competition about non-professional folk.
explanation.definitionFit: A team competition where runners take turns over stages is a contest.

clue.text: Miss coming back to control international plant

indicators.note: to control is to hold, so the reversed word holds the I
the word for miss is read backwards in this across clue

parts.note: a miss is a young woman, a lass

explanation.surface: A young woman returns to run a global factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns LASS to SSAL, and 'to control' sets I inside after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: An agave grown for its fibre, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Slip and fall, knocking out officer

indicators.note: knocking out says the officer is removed from the longer word

parts.note: to collapse is to fall down
Col is short for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: Tripping and tumbling, so an officer is floored.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip, a small error or failure of concentration.

clue.text: Libertine breaks 10 rules

indicators.note: breaks says the letters of both pieces are smashed and reset

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, the nymph of myth

explanation.surface: A rake breaks ten rules.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is a cross-reference to 10 across, ECHO; 'breaks' rearranges ECHO with RULES. Libertine works as an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, libertine means dissolute, given to lust and sexual excess.

clue.text: Spot boxes where divers hope not to get spotted

definitions.meaning: on a football pitch each penalty spot sits inside a marked box

definitions.text: where divers hope not to get spotted
definitions.meaning: footballers who dive to win a penalty do it in these zones, hoping the referee misses it

explanation.surface: Boxes for spotting where swimmers hope to stay unseen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' suggests swimmers; here they are footballers who fake a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: The marked areas in front of each goal in football, containing the penalty spot.

clue.text: What Box and Cox do about hosting Carol no end

indicators.note: hosting says the short word holds the other inside

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: no end means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a carol is a hymn sung at Christmas

explanation.surface: What a famous pair do around a Christmas song cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Box and Cox is a Victorian farce whose two title lodgers share a room; their names are words that chime.
explanation.definitionFit: Box and Cox are names that chime, so they sound alike at the end.

clue.text: Assistant's first to finish almost perfect plan

indicators.note: to finish places the picked letter at the end
almost means the word stops short of its full length

parts.note: ideal means perfect

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Assistant's

explanation.surface: An aide's priority is to complete a nearly flawless scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts IDEAL to IDE; 'to finish' puts the A from 'Assistant's first' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or scheme, a plan for what to do.

clue.text: Bank in Edinburgh daring to sack 5

indicators.note: to sack is to dismiss, so the numeral is thrown out

parts.note: brave means daring
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank bold enough to fire five staff.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5 down but is just the Roman numeral V.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is a Scottish word for a hillside or steep bank.

clue.text: Flag of Ireland Hungary banned

indicators.note: banned says the letter for Hungary is excluded

parts.note: Irish means of Ireland
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: Ireland's flag is outlawed in Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner but a plant: the yellow flag is a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, so flag is a common name for the plant.

clue.text: Many bribed corrupt person responsible for tots

indicators.note: corrupt says the letters are debased into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lots of people bribed a dishonest childcare worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks after small children while their parents are away.

clue.text: Classic garment in Friendly Islands (bar November)

indicators.note: bar means except, so the letter is left out

parts.note: the Friendly Islands is the old name for Tonga
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Traditional dress in the Pacific islands, except in November.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose robe of ancient Rome, a garment of the classical world.

clue.text: Study English judge jailing, say, reprobate

indicators.note: jailing says the combined letters lock the example inside

parts.note: a den is a private study
say means for example, abbreviated eg
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: An English judge studies, then imprisons a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jailing' puts EG inside DENERATE, just after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A degenerate is a morally corrupt person, much like a reprobate.
